sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_exact: NOT TOLERATED: ncAA mutant was not efficiently labelled. validation_level function_only -> function_perturbed. Paper (PMID 37693391): "we tested incorporation at four positions, R455, V457, K464 and T468 ... TRPV1-K464Tet3-Bu-GFP and TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP produced robust, capsaicin-activated currents". Audit note: Construct is rat TRPV1 (Julius lab cDNA), not human as the row states; rat R455/V457/K464/T468 are all confirmed in O35433 and the loop is offset -1 vs human (rat RPVEGLPPYKLKNT 455-468 = human RPVDGLPPFKMEKT 456-469), so rat K464 = human K465 and the row's 464|465 junction is right. ncAA substitution, not insertion. 'TRPV1-K464Tat3-Bu-GFP was not efficiently labelled' so surface labeling was not achieved.] Paper numbering K464 maps to canonical K465 (Q8NER1) by the same +1 offset confirmed computationally for all four screened positions. The ncAA is AT K465, so the tag junction is between F464 and K465 (insert_after_residue=464). K465 is 11 residues from TM1 end (454) and 7 residues from TM2 start (472), well within the ≥3-residue constraint. Function was preserved (capsaicin currents), but surface labeling efficiency was poor in follow-up, making this a lower-confidence site than T469. Full-length human TRPV1 expressed in HEK293T/17 cells with amber-codon suppression to incorporate a tetrazine-reactive ncAA at position K464 (paper numbering; canonical K465) in the S1-S2 extracellular loop, combined with a C-terminal GFP fusion. Screened alongside R455, V457, and T468 (paper numbering).

sources.claim: We found that TRPV1-K464Tet3-Bu-GFP and TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP produced robust, capsaicin-activated currents when interrogated with whole-cell patch-clamp Figure 3 – figure supplement 1A – B ), whereas TRPV1-R455Tet3-Bu-GFP and TRPV1-V457Tet3-Bu-GFP of incorporation did not (data not shown).

sites.functional_impact_measured: Whole-cell patch-clamp confirmed robust capsaicin-activated currents (TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP); surface labeling confirmed by sTCO-Cy5 co-localising with GFP fluorescence in HEK293T/17 cells. Ca2+ imaging also confirmed functional surface expression.
sites.rationale: The papers (PMC10491195, PMC11244879, PMC11338283) cite position T468 in the S1-S2 extracellular loop; Python search confirms this corresponds to canonical T469 (Q8NER1), with a consistent +1 offset throughout the paper's numbering (R455→R456, V457→V458, K464→K465, T468→T469). The ncAA is incorporated AT T469, so the junction for an epitope-tag insert is between K468 and T469 (insert_after_residue=468). T469 is 3 residues from TM2 (472) and 15 residues from TM1 (454), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-boundary constraint. This is the primary validated site: both surface accessibility (sTCO-Cy5 labeling) and channel function (capsaicin-evoked currents) were confirmed in the full-length membrane-anchored construct. Full-length human TRPV1 expressed in HEK293T/17 cells with amber-codon suppression to incorporate a tetrazine-reactive ncAA at position T468 (paper numbering; canonical T469) in the S1-S2 extracellular loop, combined with a C-terminal GFP fusion. The construct was screened among four S1-S2 loop positions (R455, V457, K464, T468 in paper numbering) for surface accessibility and functional tolerance.

sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_exact: insert_after_residue NULL -> 606: the paper pins the junction on human canonical Q8NER1 (paper numbering: ortholog:rat, construct species: rat). Paper (PMID 39005265): "Our TRPV1-exCellHalo construct contains a modified turret domain between transmembrane domain S5 and the pore helix with adequate space for the cpHaloTag to be accessible from the extracellular space in the fully assembled TRPV1 tetramer (Figure 4A). ... fragment set 5'-aggatgggaagaataactctgcctttgcccgcg-3'; 5'-ggtgtggactccataggcagcccggcaaattctggcc-3' and vector set 5'-aatggccagaatttgccgggctgcctatggagtccacacca-3'; 5'-aaggtctcgcgggcaaaggcagagttattcttcccatcctcaatcagtg-3'". Audit note: Recoverable from the Gibson primers: they translate to ...LIEDGKNNS|AFAR(cpHaloTag)...PEFAG|LPMESTP..., so cpHaloTag (pCAG-HASAP, Addgene 138325) is inserted between rat TRPV1 (O35433) S606 and L607 with no deletion. Rat S606 = human Q8NER1 S606 (VVTLIEDGKNDS|LPSESTSHRWRG), offset 0, so insert_after = 606 in the S5-pore turret (human 600-658). Surface: live HEK293T/17 labeling with cell-impermeant Alexa660-HaloTag ligand in 5 min. Function: capsaicin Ca2+ imaging and dose-response electrophysiology 'nearly overlapped with wild-type'. ~300-aa insertion; bioRxiv text as mirrored in PMC11244879.] L14 explicitly reports a cpHaloTag domain insertion into the extracellular turret loop of full-length membrane-anchored TRPV1, with the tag confirmed accessible from the extracellular space in the assembled tetramer. The turret spans canonical residues 600-658 (EXTRACELLULAR_3 landmark), flanked by TM5 (577-599) and TM6 (659-687). No specific junction residue is named in the clip, so insert_after_residue is left null and the region is recorded. The cpHaloTag (~297 aa) is far larger than a short epitope tag, demonstrating that this loop tolerates very large insertions. Full-length human TRPV1 (TRPV1-exCellHalo construct) expressed in HEK293T/17 cells with a circularly permutated HaloTag (cpHaloTag, ~33 kDa domain) engineered into the turret domain between TM5 (S5) and the pore helix. The paper describes the turret as having 'adequate space for the cpHaloTag to be accessible from the extracellular space in the fully assembled TRPV1 tetramer'. No specific junction residue is named in the ledger clip.

sources.claim: Our TRPV1-exCellHalo construct contains a modified turret domain between transmembrane domain S5 and the pore helix with adequate space for the cpHaloTag to be accessible from the extracellular space in the fully assembled TRPV1 tetramer ( Figure 4A ).
